voice.speaker: antinous
voice.caption: Bold-tongued Telemachus, do not lay your blame at our door. It is not the suitors who are at fault but your own mother, that queen of cunning; three years now, and nearly four, she has cheated the hearts of the Achaeans.

voice.speaker: antinous
voice.caption: She set up her great loom in the hall, a shroud, she told us, for the lord Laertes, so no woman of the land could reproach her if he lay in death without a winding-sheet. All day she wove at that web, and every night, with torches set beside her, she unraveled it thread by thread.

voice.speaker: antinous
voice.caption: Send her back to her father Icarius, and let her marry the man he names, and the man she chooses.

keys.beat: Antinous rejects Telemachus's charge and blames Penelope for prolonging the courtship.
He recounts how she wove Laertes's shroud by day and secretly unraveled it by night.
Antinous demands that Telemachus send his mother back to Icarius to choose a husband.
